purpose: One canonical redraw request: Nothosaurus needs the long neck the research describes. Requested, not yet drawn.
note: Status is deliberately 'requested-not-yet-drawn' rather than 'candidate-awaiting-human-greenlight'. Only the latter reopens a subject in tools/triassic/apply-selections.mjs, and Nothosaurus is delivered with a human-approved body: nothing here may put its caution sign back or unsettle that approval. The moment a candidate is actually drawn, the record for it takes the candidate status and the subject reopens then, on purpose.

nothosaurus.requiredFeature: a neck about a fifth of total length, distinct from the shoulders
nothosaurus.reviewerNote: The research is explicit that Nothosaurus has a long neck (19 cervicals in N. mirabilis) and the greenlit pose draws the head almost on the shoulders. The body built from it is faithful to the pose, so the pose is what is wrong.

evidence.measuredOnTheShippedBody: Two landmarks in public/assets/triassic/creatures/nothosaurus.glb agree on where the head begins: the `skull` bone's head at glTF z +1.775 and the lower-jaw mesh's first vertex at z +1.775. Behind it the last of the shoulder mass sits at z +1.55 (half-width 1.40, flippers out) and the first narrow slice at z +1.625 (half-width 0.40). The visible neck is therefore about 0.17 of a 5.00 body — a thirtieth of the animal.
evidence.whyItCannotBeFixedDownstream: tools/triassic/creatures/nothosaurus/neck-study.py stretches the neck band and renders the result (neck-study.jpg). Reaching nothosaur proportions is a factor of five to seven on a band 0.17 long: the UVs smear into a blank untextured sock, the jaw-hinge tissue that straddles the band tears, and only one and a half bones lie forward of the band so the front half of the new neck stays rigid with the skull. A stretch cannot invent cervical anatomy.
evidence.research: docs/triassic/research.md — 'Long neck (19 cervicals in N. mirabilis)'; N. mirabilis 3–4 m adult, N. giganteus 5–7 m.

nothosaurus.proportionTarget: Measured snout tip to tail tip along the body: head about an eighth, neck about a fifth, trunk (shoulder girdle to hip) about three tenths, tail the remaining third or so. The neck must read as a distinct slender run between the shoulders and a small flat skull — not a thickening of the chest, and not a swan's curve either: nothosaur necks are long but low-slung and only moderately flexible, held roughly in line with the body while swimming.
nothosaurus.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this existing canonical Nothosaurus paleoart image. Preserve EXACTLY: this individual animal's species and identity, its dark mottled olive-and-charcoal hide and every marking on it, the small flat low skull with slender rostrum and interlocking premaxillary fangs meshing visibly with the mouth shut, the broad flat wing-shaped upper forelimb bones, all four webbed paddle-like feet with distinct separate digits, the long finned tail, the underwater setting, the lighting, the camera angle and the framing. Change ONE thing and nothing else: LENGTHEN THE NECK. In the current image the head sits almost directly on the shoulders; the animal must instead have a long, distinctly slender neck carrying the small head well forward of the shoulder girdle — about one fifth of the animal's total snout-to-tail-tip length, so that head, neck, trunk and tail read as roughly one eighth, one fifth, three tenths and one third of the body. The neck is LOW-SLUNG and held roughly in line with the body axis, gently and only slightly curved, NOT raised, NOT an S-curve, NOT a swan or plesiosaur neck: Nothosaurus necks are long but stiff-ish and moderately flexible. The neck is clearly narrower than the chest and tapers smoothly from the shoulders to the base of the skull, with no abrupt step or collar where it meets either. Keep the head SMALL — do not enlarge the skull to match the longer neck. Do not lengthen the trunk, the tail or the limbs, and do not move the limbs. The whole animal stays comfortably inside the frame with the complete tail visible; if lengthening the neck would push the snout out of frame, scale the whole animal down slightly rather than cropping it. Photorealistic paleoart matching the input's quality and palette, landscape 1536x1024. No labels, no text, no people, no additional animals.
nothosaurus.consequences: This is an UPDATE to a delivered animal, not an outstanding reconstruction ask: the shipped body matches the pose it was greenlit from, which is the bar for carrying no caution sign. Acting on it means a fresh greenlight, a fresh four-view modelling sheet, a fresh Tripo generation and a rebuilt pair — and the shipped authored skin embeds the original Tripo albedo byte for byte (see tools/triassic/creatures/nothosaurus/README.md), so a regeneration draws a new skin and the animal will not be pixel-identical afterwards. Worth doing for the defining anatomy of the genus; worth knowing before it starts.
